meta.title: Hyaluronic Acid-Based 3D Bioprinted Hydrogel Structure for Directed Axonal Guidance and Modeling Innervation In Vitro.

extracted_by: Claude (Claude Code session), pending human review
summary: Soft and stiff hyaluronic acid bioinks were printed together to guide axons from stem cell-derived neurons, as a model of how nerves innervate tissue. The soft ink with NGF and laminin formed channels for axon growth.

formulations.review_notes: Pressure converted from 0.7 bar (soft ink); stiff ink 2.3 bar at 19.0 mm/s. Neurons are hPSC-derived (ESC or iPSC not captured).
formulations.name: Soft HA bioink + NGF + laminin (axon guidance)
formulations.composition_detail: Soft HA-based bioink supplemented with NGF and laminin; paired with a stiff HA bioink for structure
formulations.key_outcome: hPSC-derived neurons formed 3D networks in the soft ink with guidance cues, while the stiff ink restricted them.

evidence.quote: pressures of 0.7 bar and 2.3 bar, speeds of 15.1 mm s−1 and 19.0 mm s−1
32 G (inner Ø 100 µm) blunt needles 0.50 inches in length (CellInk, USA) were used for printing.
human pluripotent stem cell (hPSC) ‐derived neurons form a 3D neuronal network in the softer bioink supplemented with guidance cues
